quest.title: Darkness Looming
quest.description: The situation in Sumeru is even more dire than first thought, and people have come together to come up with plans for various contingencies.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1225, Mora x53900, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x10

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon: Act X
chapter.title: Of Myriad Paths, Flux, and Dissolution

talks.objective: Wait for the researcher to arrive

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: You must be the ones tasked by the Akademiya with renovating Aaru?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: That's right. Good afternoon, I'm Kaveh, and these two are Termezi and Naysaburi. Hey, Alhaitham! Come and introduce yourself...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: We've met before. This is Thoth, the Ibis King, and everyone knows these two. Afternoon, gentlemen.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I've only ever seen "these two" in murals!

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Ah, the paintings in the temple! They show us chatting, playing cards, playing chess... Precisely the activities we most enjoy, funnily enough.

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: No, only you enjoy playing chess! We were just humoring you!

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: I wouldn't go that far.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Back to the matter at hand. A preliminary assessment by the Akademiya indicates that this project requires expertise in various disciplines, including the deciphering of ancient texts, mechanical engineering, the restoration of ancient ruins, and elemental theory.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The most capable minds in their respective fields are here before you. If there are no objections, we'd like to begin our work.

dialogues.speaker: Bennu
dialogues.text: The artisans who built Aaru for Al-Ahmar gave their very lives to create this splendid work. Follow their example by giving your utmost devotion to this project.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I didn't know that. We'll do our best, of course, but we certainly won't be sacrificing our lives.

dialogues.speaker: Bennu
dialogues.text: Such brazen words! Hmph, humans these days are a far cry from their ancestors. What little respect you show for King Deshret...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: No no no, that's not what he meant! Please, don't mind him! He shares your sentiments, just not your... uh, penchant for hyperbole. Assuming that's what you were going for?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I just think it's important to manage expectations.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Forgive my lack of courtesy, but we simply can't sacrifice our lives to the gods on completion of the project like people in the legends of old.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Here's a first draft of the project proposal for your perusal. Please let us know if you have any requests.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Normally, I'd have made it look a lot more visually appealing, but... we were really pressed for time on this occasion. I hope you'll forgive me if it's a little rough around the edges.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Naturally, naturally.

dialogues.speaker: Bennu
dialogues.text: Hmph... If my fellow ministers deem this meager display of respect sufficient, I suppose I can consider agreeing to their proposal.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Why are you so preoccupied with the ostentatious displays of respect to Al-Ahmar? We should be trying to make things easy for them. You never know, we might have to rely on these young people to look after us in our old age.

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: Exactly!

dialogues.speaker: Bennu
dialogues.text: This is Aaru's mainframe. Be reminded to use it with great caution.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: We certainly will. Thank you for your assistance.

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: You may attempt to lay out punishments should you so desire, though I'm afraid it would be futile. You and I both know that certain components of Aaru can only be operated by humans.

dialogues.speaker: Bennu
dialogues.text: King Deshret always believed in humanity. Still, the reason that Aaru's modules are designed that way is not so much because he trusted them... but more because he was wary of you.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: (Is that true? No wonder human artisans helped to build Aaru, then... He actually required human assistance to create his greatest work.)

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Naturally.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Have you noticed that the Goat King keeps giving superficial responses? It's like he's just going through the motions and leaving the real debate to his colleagues.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: He understands the art of perfunctory speech — that's what earned him his position as the Minister of Ministers. It seems the rumors about King Deshret being a poor judge of character are baseless after all.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Excuse me for being blunt, but it sounds suspiciously like you're putting yourself on a pedestal and mocking me.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You're mistaken. And while there's nothing strictly wrong with making every conversation about yourself, it's not exactly a positive tendency either.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: You...! Ugh, whatever, I knew it'd be like this working with you... Alright, lemme past! I need to look at this console...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: It's your job to activate it, after all. Let's begin.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Everyone, please proceed with the external checks and preparations as per the procedures outlined in the engineering plan.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Hello there, youngsters.

dialogues.speaker: Termezi
dialogues.text: Whoa! The Ibis King came to life!

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: What do you mean "came to life"? I've been alive the whole time!

dialogues.speaker: Naysaburi
dialogues.text: Y—You did say we could start our research, right...? Are you having second thoughts now?

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: I've reviewed the proposal. The work you're planning to carry out on this grand device is ambitious in its scope. You have ample confidence in your abilities, I take it?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Haha, I wouldn't say I'm feeling hugely confident... But given how bad things are, I'd rather at least try something than sit around waiting to die.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: You are the top scholars of your day. I trust you are aware that there are countless links between Aaru and the Akasha?

dialogues.speaker: Naysaburi
dialogues.text: Aaru and the Akasha? But...

dialogues.speaker: Termezi
dialogues.text: I thought the Akasha was the Akademiya's greatest technological accomplishment? Created years ago by the Dendro Archon to help her people access knowledge...

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: And you two? Do you not know either?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: You've read the instruction manual, right? You tell them.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: An instruction manual? The Akasha has an instruction manual? The Dendro Archon is a kind and thoughtful god indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: It used to sit on a shelf in the corner at the House of Daena. Not the most popular read.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: If the manual is to be believed, Aaru was in fact the original inspiration for the Akasha system.

dialogues.speaker: Naysaburi
dialogues.text: What!? But there are so few records about Aaru anywhere... And practically none of the scientific expeditions into the desert had anything to do with it.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Ah, but this is something you could not possibly have known. You may have heard many stories about the desert, but what is the most important aspect of history? Consider this a quiz. Anyone from Vahumana present?

dialogues.speaker: Termezi
dialogues.text: I'm from Vahumana. It's, well... veracity.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Precisely. And a large part of veracity is the chronological order in which events occur.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: I may as well tell you. In the beginning, Nabu Malikata, the Goddess of Flowers, descended upon Sumeru. The glory of the heaven was within her. She brought life, oases, and knowledge to this land.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Then, she created the Jinn, enlightened them, and ordered them to serve her. Two other gods also walked upon this land where wisdom flowed in abundance, and the three met beneath the great green trees.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: It was the first and greatest alliance. We should speak with reverence of this covenant between the three, which transcended both time and life. For they promised that in Sumeru, wisdom would be shared with all.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: All the great changes in Sumeru's history began with the Goddess of Flowers. For King Deshret's sake, she pried into the secrets of Celestia, and for this was burned to ashes by the flames of wrath.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: So grieved was King Deshret by her passing that he lost all interest in state affairs and devoted himself instead to the knowledge that she had brought back. It was after learning of the technology from that floating island in the sky that he first conceived of "Aaru."

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: And so, the Akasha was inspired by Aaru, while the basis for Aaru itself came from Celestia's technology.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Well, if the two share a common technological origin... then connecting one system to the other is an entirely feasible idea.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Hmph. Unbelievable... Have you no reverence at all for celestial technology?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: No, I do, but there's no time for that! The schedule is too tight. Blame it on the deadline!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Perhaps you could try coming up with our cut-off dates.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Do you know what it's like having to turn around five different drafts in one day? I wouldn't wish it on my worst enemy!

dialogues.speaker: Termezi
dialogues.text: Yeah... Also, Sir Ibis King... You don't plan on getting directly involved at all, do you?

dialogues.speaker: Naysaburi
dialogues.text: Yes, well, you strike us more as having come to give a popular science lecture... Or wait, does this count as more of a.... firsthand witness statement?

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Ahahaha... Neither! Anyway, this sounds like far too much work for me.

dialogues.speaker: Termezi
dialogues.text: Still... if Aaru is so powerful, why didn't King Deshret use it for more ambitious ends?

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Because it was never fully completed. King Deshret had grand plans, but he perished before they could come to fruition.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: In the beginning, his wish was to create something that could rival the very world itself. The Lord of Flowers sacrificed everything for that ambition.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: What he desired, she bestowed, and thus was knowledge brought into the world. Her courage and sacrifice had to be honored with the most splendid of monuments, or King Deshret would surely have deemed it a grave injustice.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: And that monument, built from knowledge and technology, etched with a sacrificial and courageous love... Even in its unfinished form, it deserves to be treasured.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: At that time, King Deshret said the following to the Lord of Dendro:

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: "Since we share an eternal covenant, I shall never be your enemy. Hence, the fruit of wisdom from the heavens is not to be devoured."

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: "Remember, it is not that I lack the power to become the enemy of wisdom. Yet, you and she have taught me much and shown me kindness... For this, I cherish you both."

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: In the end, Aaru was only used to store a portion of the souls. It was but a primitive form of the masterwork the King had envisaged... His final hope for Aaru was to return to the past, when she yet lived.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: So the point you're making is, King Deshret was both powerful and ambitious, and he only ceased his imperious ways out of affection for the Goddess of Flowers and the Dendro Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You could see this as an act of mercy, but you could also see it as the sentiments that lay between these three gods placing constraints on him. This was, after all, the foundation of the alliance between them.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...This explains why Aaru was both a prison and a monument, and why the answer to the three questions was "time"...

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: You have to be careful who you get involved with, or you invite all manner of misfortune... This is as true for gods as it is for humans.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Love is the same. It is both a prison and a monument.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Alright, let us pause the story here for now. Seeing as you've been so diligent, I'll offer a little help.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Who's in charge again? Is it you two?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Ah, yes, me and him.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Now then, close your eyes...

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: "Wisdom hides in the space between the tangible and the intangible. It is to convey the incommunicable through the simplest of mediums."

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: "By the power of King Deshret, I shall grant you a glimpse into the unseen secrets that lie at the threshold of existence."

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...Where did this come from? Is it a new mechanism?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: It looks more like some form of externalized information... You've rendered it visible?

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Just as the Akasha allows you to access a greater range of knowledge, the power of our King permits one to perceive ingenuities that do not belong to this world.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: This is no ordinary mechanism. It reflects the internal structure of Aaru.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Whether you choose to increase or decrease, keep or discard... Come, use these to achieve the outcome you desire.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Hmm, looks mechanical to me... Better let me handle it, just in case. But wait, how do I get up there?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Turn around.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: So that's where the elevator is!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: How's it going? Are things progressing smoothly?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Well enough, I suppose. You know how it is — the work itself is only half the problem. The other half is having to work with Alhaitham.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I'm sure the feeling is mutual. Honestly, though? I thought you two had already worked things out.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: As if! Turns out working closely together is the best way to expose any tensions lurking beneath the surface... Besides...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...*sigh* I just think that some people never change.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Agreed. Case in point — you didn't make sure I was out of earshot before you started complaining about me.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Old habits die hard.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Actually, this is for your own good! Maybe if you spend a little more time listening to what other people have to say, you might actually realize that you're the problem!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Naivete is another old habit of yours.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I had assumed that you both volunteered for this project, like us Forest Rangers... But now I'm getting the sense that wasn't the case.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Definitely not. We were assigned to it by Lesser Lord Kusanali and Naphis.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: *sigh* As much as I'd love to be doing normal work for normal clients, these titan projects are all that's on offer right now. Though I'm sure they wouldn't be roping us in if they had any better options... Just goes to show how short-staffed the Akademiya really is.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I'm sure you've prepared yourself mentally, but I still feel the need to advise you to lower your expectations. It might make the process of working together a little less intolerable.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I know! Same to you! But if you already understood that, you should also know not to say the quiet part out loud!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Why don't you come help me with my forest patrols? Might help you avoid any further disagreements.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Good suggestion, but unfortunately, differences of opinion will always exist. Changing the nature of the work won't get rid of them.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: For once, I actually agree. There is zero chance of us ever resolving our differences! Zero!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...But even so, the work must be done. *sigh*... Care for some coffee?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I'm glad to see you making progress.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Don't act so smug! It'd be nice if you made some, too!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I feel like even I've made some progress today. In the past, I never would have dared to try and mediate a conflict between you two while you're both right there in front of me.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Apologizing probably makes it sound like I'm in the wrong, but... I'm sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Heh, I was just kidding. Truth be told, I don't have any work to do at the moment, so I'm just here to kill some time.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: How's Collei?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: She's studying with Nicole. I'm not sure how she's getting along... but she seems to be in good spirits, at least.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I wouldn't worry. Angelic affairs are probably above your pay grade anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I know what you mean, but Cyno and I are still a little concerned for her. He said he'd go keep Collei company after he's finished training the mercenaries. I'm planning to join them myself shortly.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Collei will be okay. Have faith in her.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Even we can see how much more confident and outgoing she's become in these past few years. Thanks to you and Cyno being there for her and providing guidance every step of the way, she can finally stand on her own two feet.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: On her own two feet...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Does it feel bittersweet watching the younger generation grow up and move on?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: No. Not yet, at least. I was just thinking... I wish there was more I could do for everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: She'll be fine.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Yeah, she will. Just try to relax.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Obelisks were used to record important information in the ancient desert civilization... Hey, Alhaitham, there's some writing here I'll need you to decipher.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I've sent it to your screen. Do you see it?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Got it... It's a little blurry, but I should manage.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Take a look and tell me what it says. Oh, and I'll send any other similar text directly to you from now on.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Let's start with this one. Hmm, it's a variant of an older script... "Herein lie verses written for the yellow sands."

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Looks like cultural information from the age of King Deshret.

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: Ahem... If so, I suggest you delete it.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Haha... Words thrown together merely for fun. I had no idea Aaru kept a record of this.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Well, as long as you're certain that this is strictly private information, that's fine.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: It is unimportant.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Alright, well... I guess I'll start now.

dialogues.speaker: Arapas
dialogues.text: Waaaah... Big Dendro Dragon threw us across the sky... so scary... and so many Nara here...

dialogues.speaker: Aradashan
dialogues.text: Cheer up, Arapas, they're all looking at us! Wait... th—they're all looking at us!?

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: Surely, all those Nara can't see us...? Nara are always so busy, walking here and there...

dialogues.speaker: Arapas
dialogues.text: Hide, hide! Don't let the Nara catch us. They can have the pot, but... Wait, no! The Nara can't take the pot. My sister said I have to look after it...

dialogues.speaker: Arayuta
dialogues.text: Th—The Nara are coming...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Hello, everyone. It's only us.

dialogues.speaker: Arabalika
dialogues.text: #Oh! Lord of Dendro, Nara {NICKNAME}, and White Floaty.

dialogues.speaker: Aradashan
dialogues.text: #Lord of Dendro, Nara {NICKNAME}, Paimon! It's been a long time.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It must be very tough for you coming all the way out here, especially since you don't like the Val{RUBY#[S]sand}uka. Is everyone back in Vanarana doing well?

dialogues.speaker: Arabalika
dialogues.text: Araja is a Vasara Tree. Vasara Trees protect Vanarana, so that means Araja is protecting Vanarana.

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: Don't worry, everyone who stayed behind will do their best to protect their home. And we'll all do our part, too!

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Ah, everyone's here. Good.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you okay? You looked like you were about to pass out back there.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Hmph, then you're forgetting who I am! Don't underestimate me!

dialogues.speaker: Arapas
dialogues.text: Sorush, the mighty Red Floaty.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Red Fl— Excuse me!? Are you comparing me to Paimon!?

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: Well, Ararycan think it suits you...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I suppose everyone is gathered here because of me. As we can see, the situation is critical, and everyone is very busy with their various tasks, so—

dialogues.speaker: Arapas
dialogues.text: Need help? Arapas can help! We can all help! Arapas brought a pot to make soup. Very delicious!

dialogues.speaker: Arayuta
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm, all of us are here to help!

dialogues.speaker: Arabalika
dialogues.text: Arabalika, Ararycan, Arapas, Aradashan, Arayuta, Arasata, and Arasaha will all help!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I can't thank you enough. Right now, we're focused on restructuring Aaru, processing excess information, and helping restore everyone's confidence... I'm sure you'll find it all very straightforward.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: I can help too. Just let me know where I'm needed.

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: Together, together!

dialogues.speaker: Arabalika
dialogues.text: Lord of Dendro, Arabalika has something important to tell you.

dialogues.speaker: Arabalika
dialogues.text: On our way out of Vanarana, we saw some Nara talking in secret... Male Nara, up to no good.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Up to no good?

dialogues.speaker: Arabalika
dialogues.text: Yes... Two Nara, sneaking around. At Ca... Cara...

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: Caravan Ribat!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: ...Hmm, that definitely sounds suspicious.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, I have other work to attend to here that needs to take priority. Could I trouble you to investigate the situation Arabalika spoke of?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No problem! Leave it to us!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Thank you, I'm counting on you.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: There's one other thing. If you are to work alongside the people of Sumeru, you will need to make yourselves visible to them... Is that acceptable to everyone?

dialogues.speaker: Arapas
dialogues.text: W—Well, if we really have to...

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: ...I guess we have no choice.

dialogues.speaker: Arasata
dialogues.text: Don't be afraid, Arapas. You make the most delicious soup. Everyone will like you.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: There's nothing to fear. No one here will hurt you. But if you do feel afraid, don't worry — just call my name, and I'll be there.

dialogues.speaker: Arabalika
dialogues.text: Okay.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Very well. Now, I shall bestow a small blessing upon you all. Whenever people see you and interact with you, from the moment their gaze meets yours they will experience the most beautiful of dreams.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Nahida gently raises her hand. You don't know what she did, but you feel a wonderful presence, like something out of a lovely dream indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Sunlight trickling through the branches, glistening like gold leaf... The trees chanting softly in the breeze as the flowing water plays a symphony... Your heart swells up like a balloon as it fills with happiness.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: There are many terrible things yet to be resolved. But in this moment, all you feel is peace, friendship, and love as you stand side by side with dozens of other creatures together in the forest.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Found some more. Sending them over to you now.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: ...These are all reports about the Gurabad conflict.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Can we delete them?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I'd say so. Most of this information has already been archived anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Hmm... What if there are details in there that Vahumana missed? What are we supposed to do if they come after us in the future?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: They'll just have to live with it. If we don't resolve these issues now, there won't even be an Akademiya in the future, let alone a Vahumana Darshan.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Yeah, you're right. Okay, done.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: There's some other similar monuments nearby. I'll check them out.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: There is still much to be done. Everyone, please remember our core strategy.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: As per the discussions, the following groups must act immediately:

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Mr. Alhaitham and Mr. Kaveh, the next phase of the Aaru Renovation Project must begin right away. Godspeed to you both.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: We'll give it everything we've got.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The plan looks feasible, but the implementation will require certain resources.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: General Mahamatra Cyno and his team will help to procure the materials required for modifying the terminal.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: No problem. I've already spoken with Sethos and Hat Guy, and they've agreed to assist me.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: This kind of thing is best left to the fleet-footed, right, Hat Guy?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: If it's efficiency you're after, we're the right people for the job.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Following up on the elemental energy amplifier we discussed... Miss Dori, I assume you're the one most familiar with the status of this project? Aside from the Dendro Archon, of course?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Yup, that's right! Leave it to Lord Sangemah Bay.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Got it. Well, I'd like Madam Faruzan, Collei, and Nicole to support Dori on the technical side.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: You can count on us.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Will do!

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Rest assured, I'll take good care of Collei.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Dehya, Candace, and Nefer, you'll be in charge of negotiating between the various parties. I trust you remember our goal?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: You bet. We can handle it.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Good. I believe that covers everything. Tighnari will provide ad-hoc support as needed, if that's okay?

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Poor Tighnari. It must be tough being Naphis's student, getting bossed around all day every day.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Hey, don't try and drive a wedge between us, you old rascal.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: All it says to me is that Master Naphis has faith in everyone's abilities. While I'm nominally here as backup, I doubt there will be many situations where my help is needed.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Exactly.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #Finally... {NICKNAME}, you and I will head to the border between Sumeru and Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Once that task is complete, I'll be asking some of you to accompany me to the Eternal Oasis.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: The Eternal Oasis? I thought that was just a legend... so it does exist after all.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Regarding your trip to Natlan... Under normal circumstances, a meeting between our two nations would be a far more formal affair. Unfortunately, Sumeru is all but completely cut off from the outside world at present...

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: So regretfully, we won't be able to give the Pyro Archon Mavuika the grand reception that she deserves. My apologies for the inconvenience.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not a problem. We'll do our utmost.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: No point putting too much pressure on yourselves. That goes for everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Right! Especially you, Dendro Archon. I'm sure you're still feeling quite weak.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Don't worry about me. The Dendro Dragon's life force will sustain me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Plus, we'll be there every step of the way. Nahida will be just fine!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Yes. I believe in myself, and I believe in every one of you.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Well, time to get going.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Another monument.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Hold on.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: You're still reading it? How long is it?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: It records the development and governance of the Oasis civilization. Most of it concerns the Jinn, but it also contains records left by the artisans who built Aaru.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Is it important?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Some of it. There was no way for me to read the whole thing in its entirety, so I had to rely on my intuition to pick the parts worth keeping.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: What about the artisans' records, what do they mention?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Their speculations, mostly. For instance, they were wondering how to protect themselves if King Deshret decided to silence them after the construction of Aaru was complete.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...Sounds like pure mythology to me. Surely that kind of thing didn't really happen?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The records do emphasize that this was merely their conjecture based on various myths. Still, the artisans did leave details of their plans to survive, including blueprints for their escape route.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Even that got recorded? Okay, well I'll make a copy of this first before I delete it...

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Is that truly necessary? You won't be needing those.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: No, no, the blueprints are important. I want to keep them as a memento.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Phew, I think that should just about do it...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: It meets the requirements of the contingency plans, so we should be good.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I gotta say, it's the strangest feeling, this cross between reality and the intangible...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: It's like drifting between life and death, or in and out of a dream, using my own hands to manipulate illusions that are forever out of reach.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Chasing dreams in the most literal sense. Definitely a novel experience.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: What happens if my spirit just... floats away?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: That won't happen. Anyway, I wouldn't celebrate just yet if I were you. There's likely to be a phase two of this project.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Alright, I'd better keep my wits about me, then.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: I expected that the outside world no longer respected the ancient gods... but even so, I do find the tone of these youngsters to be dreadfully impolite.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: It should hardly come as a surprise to you. I remember you saying the same thing last time.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: I assumed that was just a one-off... I did not realize it was the norm.

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: Don't you think that young lad's matter-of-fact tone sounds familiar? It bears a rather uncanny resemblance to you, Goatie.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Surely a sign that he is a man of rare intelligence.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth & Sobek
dialogues.text: Argh!

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: Argh!

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: The rest of them, though... Much better. The blond-haired one for instance. So sincere. That's the kind of kid I can respect.

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: Oh really? Well, what about your disciple, Nefer? She's about the furthest from sincerity that a person can get.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Ah, and now you hit the crux of the issue. Thoth is spouting lies again. He cares nothing for sincerity — he likes Nefer simply because her personality is just like his.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Thus, in giving his approval to Nefer, Thoth is simply validating himself. The rest is but smoke and mirrors.

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: You have some nerve saying that. There really is no helping you two...

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf & Thoth
dialogues.text: Shut up, chess rookie.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Shut up, chess rookie.

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: What nonsense is this!? How dare you tell me to shut up!

dialogues.speaker: Bennu
dialogues.text: How can you engage in such banal chitter-chatter at a time like this? Aaru has been opened, the glory and splendor of a bygone age is about to sweep over the earth like a flood, and you're here squabbling like petulant children?

dialogues.speaker: Bennu
dialogues.text: All three of you are insufferable! King Deshret was merciful indeed, giving you a chance to be released from prison. I say, you should have been locked up for good!

dialogues.speaker: Shesepankh
dialogues.text: Ah, but Bennu, look on the bright side. Had they not been released, we would not have been awoken.

dialogues.speaker: Bennu
dialogues.text: Oh, you've been here this whole time? You should be scolding them along with me!

dialogues.speaker: Shesepankh
dialogues.text: I miss Hermanubis. It's not a real reunion without him here.

dialogues.speaker: Bennu
dialogues.text: And now you're avoiding the topic and talking to yourself... Why King Deshret designed your personality like this, I will never understand!

dialogues.speaker: Shesepankh
dialogues.text: Isn't this simply proof that our King supports my free will?

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: Look at those two rustbuckets... Suddenly, you two do not seem so bad after all.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Hear, hear. If being stuck together for thousands of years fosters no friendship, I cannot say what would.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Naturally.

talks.objective: Head to the entrance to King Deshret's mausoleum

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: Traveler from afar... Do you worry for the fate of Sumeru as well?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! It's Sobek the Crocodile King!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Greetings, Crocodile King.

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: Please be at ease. I'm just here to chat with you about Lesser Lord Kusanali.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sounds like you really care about her.

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: Yes, although to be exact... it is a mixture of both concern and curiosity that I feel.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Speaking of Nahida, Paimon was wondering how she's doing...

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: Wait a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: I tried calling out to Apep, but there was no response.

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: This can only mean that she is focusing all her energy on taking care of Lesser Lord Kusanali.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: All the gods who served King Deshret seemed super surprised to hear that Apep agreed to help Nahida... Guessing she made a bad impression on you, or something?

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: Are you aware of the history between her and our King?

response.speaker: Sobek
response.text: Then you are learned indeed. I am glad to know that Sumeru has the support of someone like you.

response.speaker: Sobek
response.text: At the end of his life, King Deshret tricked the Dendro Dragon into swallowing him whole, leaving her to bear the torment of his sins...

response.speaker: Sobek
response.text: The Dendro Dragon despised King Deshret, yet he outwitted her. Rather than bringing disaster to the land, he chose to deceive her and thereby ensure his annihilation — an act that surely displays his love for humanity.

response.speaker: Sobek
response.text: The Dendro Dragon stands for the glory of a bygone era... She hated Al-Ahmar and what he represented: all the gods, all the power they wielded.

response.speaker: Sobek
response.text: And so, her willingness to help the Dendro Archon through this crisis comes as a great surprise indeed. It makes one wonder whether, perhaps, the Dendro Archon assisted her in the past?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup, Nahida did her a huge favor!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Sobek about how Nahida helped to free Apep from her suffering...

response.speaker: Sobek
response.text: So Lesser Lord Kusanali put an end to the Dendro Dragon's many long years of torment...

response.speaker: Sobek
response.text: As much as she loathes The Seven, Apep knows kindness when she sees it. No wonder she was willing to make an exception.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, that's the sense we got from dealing with her, too.

response.speaker: Sobek
response.text: She is not incapable of coexisting with other living things — rather, she actively chooses to avoid coexistence. And this, despite the fact that she symbolizes life itself... How ironic.

response.speaker: Sobek
response.text: All of this being said, I wouldn't expect too much from her if I were you. Nothing will change her hatred towards humanity and gods.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We'll keep that in mind...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, how much longer do you think Nahida needs to stay with Apep?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Maybe we should go and pick her up?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: For all we know, the Fatui might still be in the desert... Just to be on the safe side, why don't we grab anyone who isn't busy right now and go look for her?
I'm alright, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Was that Nahida's voice?

response.speaker: Sobek
response.text: It seems the treatment was effective.
Since when do my deeds require your evaluation?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Here will do just fine.

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: I had no intention of taking you any further. One ought not expect greater generosity than they have earned.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: You always hide your kindness away like an oasis within a sandstorm. Only those who make it through the swirling winds can know just how beautiful that oasis is, and how much hope it brings.

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: You dare appraise my being?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: No, I'm expressing my gratitude. I want to thank you for sharing your precious life force with me.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Hmm...

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: Awake already? You are more resilient than I thought.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Apep...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I feel much better. Thank you.

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: Gods and their gratitude mean little to me. I would rather you give me your assurance that the situation with Irminsul and Sumeru's Ley Lines will be competently managed.

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: If I suffer any ill effects from the Ley Lines, you, as the god of this land, will be held responsible... and you would not enjoy being held to account by me.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I understand what you require. But I would assume this task even if you did not demand it.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Sumeru is my responsibility. I must resume my duties as soon as possible.

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: A farcical notion. God of Sumeru, I hope you realize how unextraordinary your strength is.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: And yet, maybe it is precisely what defines me. A God of Wisdom is not meant to rule by force.

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: Then hold steady. We go forth.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Well, I'll be... Is that Apep!?

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Do my eyes deceive me? Of all places, the Dendro Dragon has decided to visit the Mausoleum of King Deshret?

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: I see that after all this time, Al-Ahmar's menagerie of ministers remain as vile as ever.

response.speaker: Heryshaf
response.text: It's a pleasure, Dendro Dragon. Had you arrived but a little sooner, you might have attended a meeting of the Seven Pillars.

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: Pah. What a nauseating thought.

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: You are not the first insects I have had the displeasure of dealing with today. A swarm of them tugged on my tail on my way over — goodness knows what hovels they crawled from. Why do all the creatures of this world remain so lowly after all this time?

response.speaker: Sobek
response.text: What did you do with them?

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: I cast them away! What would you have me do, keep them as trinkets?

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: Buer, this is where we shall part ways. To be clear, I do not wish to see you, or anyone else here, ever again unless absolutely necessary.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Then I wish you peace as you return to your dwelling place.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thank you for helping Nahida.

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: It matters not to me. Simply refrain from bothering me again.

response.speaker: Sobek
response.text: A force to be reckoned with... At times like this, I feel glad that she has no interest in any of this.
Ugh, hold on... just hold on, okay? We're almost there!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Wait, that voice, it's...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Sorush?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: We made it!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Obviously, I was worried about the Dendro Archon! I've been supporting them with my pari powers the whole way here...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Uh-oh! I'm gonna fall!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I've got you!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Well that's a relief. A pair of safe hands indeed...

response.speaker: Heryshaf
response.text: The Dendro Archon's familiars... They are the last thing I expected to see here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Wait, what are the Aranara doing here!? Don't you guys hate the desert?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: They seem pretty nervous. Is it 'cause there are too many people around...?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Not just people! It's all these non-human beings too... It's hard on them.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I can't believe you made such a long and dangerous journey just for my sake... I appreciate your support so much. Thank you all.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I'll have to ask everyone to wait while I help our new arrivals settle in. Once I'm done, I'll gather everyone to discuss our next steps.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, shall we find a place for our friends to stay?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Awesome! Let's go!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Well, first I have some questions...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You answer Nahida's questions, bringing her up to speed on everything that has happened...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Okay, I think that covers everything... Thank you. We can get going now.

response.speaker: Sobek
response.text: The story begins a long time ago. Al-Ahmar was always a wishful thinker where the Dendro Dragon was concerned... Without consulting her, he decided to list her among the Seven Pillars and declared his own power to be far superior to hers.

response.speaker: Sobek
response.text: That was when our King was at the height of his power. Ibis, Goatie and I were no match for him, and so we chose to submit and serve as his ministers. But not Apep... No, she never thought much of him.

response.speaker: Sobek
response.text: To Apep, Al-Ahmar's pride and sense of superiority were nothing but ignorance and hubris. In fact, they fought numerous times, but usually the battle ended in a draw.

response.speaker: Sobek
response.text: In the end, King Deshret coveted the power of Celestia, only to end up corrupted by knowledge.

response.speaker: Sobek
response.text: His final act was to trick the dragon into swallowing him whole, leaving her to bear the torment of his sins...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Ah, everyone's here. Wonderful.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Dendro Archon! You're back!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Are you recovering alright? You mustn't push yourself too hard.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I'm doing very well. Thank you for your concern.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The scholars update Nahida on the progress of Aaru's renovation...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I see... Using the power of Aaru to reboot the Akasha and gain access to Irminsul.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It's a sound plan, although...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I regret to be the bearer of bad news, but with the state that Irminsul is currently in, it's impossible to access via traditional means. Even the Akasha won't change that.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: ...Alas. We had feared this may be the case.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: What about non-traditional means?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Non-traditional means?

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Are you saying...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Desperate times call for new measures.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Heyyy! We're here!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Benben and I are here to help too!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you. Is there a situation?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: The Aranara have good intuition when it comes to people. In other words, there may well be a traitor among us.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Given everything that's going on, I'd be more surprised if there wasn't.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Miss Nefer, as a professional intelligence broker, I trust you have a solution?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Not one that I'm willing to volunteer. What's in it for me?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Let's say I'll treat this as a pilot project aimed at expanding your intelligence operations. Whatever business you're in, an avenue to demonstrate your abilities could never hurt.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I like the sound of that. Glad we're on the same page.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Given that you rarely set foot in Sumeru, practically no one at Caravan Ribat knows who you are.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I take it you've read the files on everyone in the area?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Yes. I also skimmed the list of evacuees, and I'm more or less up to date on where everyone stands.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Any initial suspects?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Limiting the scope to males whose recent activity could be viewed as suspicious, I've identified three names.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: The Aranara saw two people talking, but currently we only have one suspect. The other person was probably just a messenger, and in all likelihood has already left Caravan Ribat.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Everyone is heading for the desert, per the evacuation order. Anyone willing to turn back at this stage is almost certainly with the Fatui.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: There's no way it was a spur-of-the-moment decision to act at a time like this. This spy must have been planted long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...We need to smoke him out from wherever he's hiding.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Sounds like you have the beginnings of a plan.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Cyno and Nefer quickly exchange intel and narrow down the relevant information...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...I see. Your suspicions are well-founded. I'd be watching him too if I were you.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: So far, we still lack solid evidence that he's been bribed. He hasn't made any recent purchases that would indicate he came into some cash.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Then let's get closer to him to confirm before we make our move. I can handle it — I'm not based in Sumeru, so barely anyone at Caravan Ribat knows who I am.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: And you're certain you've never encountered this person in Nod-Krai?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I'm certain. Besides, it's extremely rare for me to have had any direct contact with Sumeru mercenaries besides Jeht. There's no way he could have seen my face before.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Cyno, stay out of sight and wait for my signal. If he raises any red flags, I'll bring him toward the main road.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Understood. I'll take it from there.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Excellent. Well, it's a pleasure working with you.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Ahh! Fresh air... A wondrous feeling.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Naturally.

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: Ah, I have a sudden urge to stretch my legs... Can anyone recommend a suitable leisure activity?

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: I might have had some recommendations for you, were this the past. But here and now, for someone who has just left prison... there could be no greater joy than simply being outside of it at last.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: I could not agree more.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: As I thought, the so-called Seven Pillars of King Deshret are as underwhelming as ever.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: What do you mean? Not a fan of the boys' club?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: As men, as individuals, and even as gods, they are entirely undeserving of my attention.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Al-Ahmar once commanded me to select a king from among the people, so naturally, my eyes will open only for one who is worthy.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Ugh... Can we talk about something else? It all sounds pretty complicated, and I haven't read that many storybooks...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Hah, you think this is a mere story? Well, many would also say that the journey you shared with your father is naught but a tale. My life, your life... they are nothing but stories.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: ...Little girl, it appears that you really have grown. In the past, you would have flown into a blind rage at my words, but now you are unperturbed.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Oh, it's nothing. I just feel like you're right.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Getting all pissed at someone for telling the truth is pointless. It only makes me look petty.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: This alone is proof enough of your growth. You're doing well, my dear girl. You're becoming ever stronger — strong enough to defend the people and things you hold dear.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: ...You think so...? I hope you're right.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (...A coin? Interesting. Could that be how his contact paid him? Conveniently discreet for someone trying to hide any unexplained income, and yet it could be highly valuable...)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Sorry to bother you. Has everyone here already left? I don't suppose you happened to see a lady wearing a hat?

dialogues.speaker: Qanafiya
dialogues.text: Ma'am? What are you doing in Caravan Ribat all by yourself? The main group evacuated some time ago. Didn't you pass them on the road?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: My friend and I lost some of our cargo along the way. I didn't want to miss out on potential business, so I told her to go on ahead and meet the client while I retraced our steps. I didn't think it would be so late by the time I found it...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: *sigh* And then there was a terrible sandstorm... I guess I must have taken a wrong turn, because I didn't see any large groups on my way here.

dialogues.speaker: Qanafiya
dialogues.text: Forgive me for asking, but just to be on the safe side... Could you describe this friend of yours?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Sure — she has blonde hair, and she was wearing a hat and a white dress. You'd definitely know if you'd seen her.

dialogues.speaker: Qanafiya
dialogues.text: Yes, I think that does ring a bell... Ah, my apologies. During this exceptional time, the Corps of Thirty are under orders to be extra cautious when dealing with unknown people, whoever they might be.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I understand. Well, Sir, is there anything else you need to know? If not, I'd better try and catch up with them.

dialogues.speaker: Qanafiya
dialogues.text: Hey, wait!

dialogues.speaker: Qanafiya
dialogues.text: They left a good while ago now. You'll never catch up with them on your own. Why don't I give you a ride? I'm here to collect the last few people anyway. We have plenty of carts, so one more won't be a problem.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: That would be amazing! Traveling with a group will be much safer. I'll have to pay you for your trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Qanafiya
dialogues.text: Hey, let's not worry about the money for now. Wait here a moment. Once I'm done packing up, I'll take you to join the rest of the group.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Alright, thanks. Let me know if you need a hand carrying anything.

dialogues.speaker: Qanafiya
dialogues.text: Hahaha, no need for that. I'm strong enough for both of us.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Okay. Well, I wish there was some way I could repay you... Guess it's my lucky day, running into someone who knows what they're doing here. You might have just saved my life, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Qanafiya
dialogues.text: You're not wrong there. I mean, what kind of cargo is so important that it's worth risking your life to get back? I hope for your sake that it's priceless...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Um... actually...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...I suppose I can tell you, since you've been such a big help. But be sure to keep it to yourself, or we could both be in big trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Qanafiya
dialogues.text: Oh, really? Sounds mysterious.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: We're in the... antiques business. You understand? Some of our goods aren't acquired through the most legitimate means. We have to be very discreet when we're selling them. That's why I had to go looking for the missing cargo alone.

dialogues.speaker: Qanafiya
dialogues.text: Ah, no wonder...

dialogues.speaker: Qanafiya
dialogues.text: ...Well, Ma'am, in that case, it turns out that maybe there is something you could do for me.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I'm all ears — but to be clear, our commission isn't cheap. Think carefully before you ask. We don't want to ruin our relationship before we even hit the road.

dialogues.speaker: Qanafiya
dialogues.text: I'm sure that won't be a problem. My issue is... I have something that's a little difficult to sell on as well. Take a look at this...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The mercenary reveals the old coin in his hand. Thanks to her dealings in Nod-Krai, Nefer has seen plenty of antiques in her time and recognizes it as a very rare, high-value item.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The ancient coin used to pay off the mercenary is made of pure gold. At first glance, it's hard to discern its country of origin. If sold to a astute collector, it would fetch a very high price...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Hands where I can see them!

dialogues.speaker: Qanafiya
dialogues.text: General Mahamatra!? No, wait... wh—what are you doing!?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: This is the coin? Good.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Sadly, you won't have the chance to spend it.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Nicely done. Looks like Sumeru's matra are a well-oiled machine nowadays.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Unmarked gold coins are quite difficult to trace. Thanks to you, we have secured the evidence.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Here's what's gonna happen...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Cyno nods to the group, then turns and leaves with the suspect.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Before long, he returns with the intel he got out of the suspect...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hat Guy, wait up! Hey, slow down, will you!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: We're here. Now, we wait.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, yeah, cool... Cool.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: What's on your mind, Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Oh, uh... n—nothing...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I thought all you cared about, besides being a guide, was food and sleep. Why the sudden urge to go on a dangerous mission?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's that supposed to mean? Paimon's been on plenty of dangerous missions before!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: #But never on your own. You hardly ever leave {NICKNAME}'s side.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Ummm...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Just saying, I'm kind of at loose ends right now, so if you did wanna share, I suppose I'd have to listen. If not, suit yourself. Makes no difference to me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hat Guy... Do you... think Paimon is useless?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: What? Where's that coming from?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #When we were in Nod-Krai, Paimon suddenly realized something. Even though Paimon's with {NICKNAME} every single day, whenever we face real danger... She can't do anything to help.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon doesn't get like this very often. She just got really scared when {NICKNAME} got kidnapped that time... What if {M#he}{F#she} never came back? What would Paimon do then?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...And the more Paimon thought about it, the more useless she felt... But Paimon doesn't want to be a burden. Paimon wants to be a friend who's actually useful.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... Does that make any sense? You know that feeling of just... just being completely useless, and... Ugh, Paimon probably sounds so ridiculous right now!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You asked the right person. Boy, do I know that feeling.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw, Hat Guy...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I'm not gonna try and encourage you. What I will say is this: When you start doubting yourself, you have two choices — give up, or change.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You have to make the decision to move forward. Otherwise, no amount of consolation from other people is gonna help you.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: So ask yourself — what do you want? To get stronger? To learn more? Whatever it is, go do it. You won't have any regrets if you can at least say that you tried.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Alright!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: (...Something's not right. Shouldn't they be here by now?)

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Paimon, is it just me, or is it a little too quiet around here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, should Paimon take a look...?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: We'll give it another hour. If nothing happens, we head back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Time ticks by, but still nothing happens...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How strange... We've been here for ages, where the heck are they? Have we been stood up?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is it? Did you think of something?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Something feels off about this whole situation, but I can't quite explain why.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: We know for sure that the guy Cyno caught had something set up, yet somehow his contact is a no-show. So, either the handler got caught — or, more likely, they decided to cut our guy loose.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... how would they know to do that? Wouldn't they at least send someone here to check things out?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: That's the problem. They couldn't possibly know what's happening here, unless...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Tsk, this feels all too familiar... Come on, let's head back.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Even though this isn't a formal meeting, I'd still like to start by saying how grateful I am to each and every one of you. Thank you all for coming here and standing by our side.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Shesepankh and Bennu are currently assisting the scholars with the maintenance of Aaru. Please forgive their absence.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: As for Hermanubis, may he rest in peace. We remember him with great fondness.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: There have been times when I've imagined what it might be like to meet you all. Now that it's really happening, I feel quite emotional.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Time has taken many things away, but that which remains is all the more resilient.

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: I must say, there is one thing that rather surprises me.

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: You appear to be in good spirits, Lesser Lord Kusanali. But even so, I can sense that the life force given to you by the Dendro Dragon has far from fully resolved the problem of your vitality...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no... So even Apep's power didn't work?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Don't worry, Paimon. It worked very well indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The issue is how closely I am tied to Irminsul. Until the problem with it is resolved, there's no way I can fully recover.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Sumeru has undergone tremendous changes during your absence. When gods pass away, inevitably people's faith in them grows weaker... You must have sensed it already. Your power is not what it once was.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: *sigh*... Regrettably, this is true.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I, too, have grown weaker due to the effects of Irminsul. Right now, we're all in quite a sorry state.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Then what do you suggest?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: We take all the help we can get.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Sumeru is our shared home. You and I, gods and humans alike, we must unite all our strength in this moment.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Though Al-Ahmar is no longer with us, the alliance between the three gods remains in force. Regardless, as subjects of our King, we have a responsibility to support Sumeru through this catastrophe.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Not to mention that it was the people of Sumeru who released us from this prison of Aaru. Times have changed, and the people of today possess greater wisdom than those of the past.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Heh, you really know how to give a rousing speech, Goatie.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Now then, let us learn more about your plan.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: The brightest minds of the Sumeru Akademiya are busy opening and renovating Aaru. They claim it has something to do with Irminsul?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Correct.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Irminsul has existed in Teyvat since the very beginning. But during the age of the dragons, it did not possess the significance it holds today.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: After the Heavenly Principles arrived, the power of the Light Realm was divided into elemental energy, and Irminsul was refashioned as a device that records and preserves all information.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Since then, everything in this world has been inextricably linked to it.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: As the Dendro Archon, I have a duty to protect Irminsul. To Sumeru, it is both a national treasure and, undeniably, a major threat.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Teyvat has seen many upheavals in the last few years. The most recent of these was a major crisis in Nod-Krai, which forced Sumeru to be even more vigilant than usual.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I made sure to monitor all the pathways through which an outsider could potentially transmit themselves into Irminsul. But despite my efforts, a major problem still arose within...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I still believe that someone has actively invaded Irminsul. But rather than taking any of the pathways I referred to, the intruder chose instead to utilize the most direct route... and the only one that cannot be protected against...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: ...By entering Irminsul through death.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: I see what you mean. You cannot simply stop all deceased souls from returning to the Ley Lines because of a potential invasion that could occur at any time.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: That's right. As important as it is to guard against external threats, I couldn't allow myself to stop the souls of the departed from finding peace.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Please understand how difficult this predicament was for the Dendro Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Defense has never been an easy task.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: After Irminsul was invaded, my authority was quickly restricted. Soon after that, the tree began denying access to any connections...

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: I'm sure you feel responsible, but you are not to blame. No one can predict every possible disaster. There will always be trials and tribulations for the world to endure.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But the people of Sumeru should not have to endure this. We must find a way to break through the lockdown and connect to Irminsul.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: And this is why you need Aaru.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Yes. The only thing in Sumeru capable of rivaling Irminsul in terms of overall function and performance is Al-Ahmar's legacy — Aaru.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: All I managed to do before falling into a coma was make some minor adjustments to Irminsul. Using Aaru is a last resort, and a move that comes with enormous risks.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The scholars' initial plan was to borrow Aaru's power to reboot the Akasha, then use the Akasha to connect to Irminsul and investigate.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, Irminsul has suffered far greater damage than they first thought, rendering that plan futile.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: To rise to the challenge, we had to resort to more extreme and far costlier means. This has led to a number of new contingency plans.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: To reclaim Irminsul, our brightest scholars have made further modifications to Aaru with multiple goals in mind. I thank you all for giving them your blessing in this endeavor.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Human wisdom has clearly improved over the millennia. You have not only our support, but that of the Jinn, the aranara, and the pari.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Together, we will do everything in our power to save Irminsul.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: By the way... When you spoke earlier of an intruder, it almost sounded as if you knew who you were dealing with, and what they were capable of.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Well... since you ask...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Master Tighnari... Wh—What is that?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Is this... Irminsul?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: How did this happen!? What's going on inside?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Luckily, we managed to evacuate everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What in the world was that!? That was... terrifying...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Nahida... So this is the catastrophe she's been fighting against all this time?)

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Oh my... I understand now, Dendro Archon. You make yourself quite clear indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: Not once over the millennia has Irminsul been so terribly afflicted as this...

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: ...Please continue, Dendro Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Irminsul's root system is what comprises the Ley Lines. In the past, it has always been hidden away, going unseen by the general populace. But now, an evil intruder is making it reveal itself.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It has become a tree of unbridled greed... a clear sign that a deranged experiment has advanced to a new stage.
Blasphemy... From where I stand, an experiment in the name of blasphemy sounds rather improper.
But if we are to honor Dottore's will, this is what we must do.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The birth of this tree proves to me beyond doubt that this incident is connected to him.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But to explain the situation in full, there is someone I need to tell you about...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: In the most concise and precise language possible, Nahida explains what she knows about the Second of the Fatui Harbingers, The Doctor.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: His true name is Zandik, and his crimes are beyond all reckoning.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Zandik... So it was him. I saw him in the desert once... A man of supreme arrogance... So this is where it has taken him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But didn't Dottore die in Nod-Krai? How is he still able to do all this?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: He must still have loyal followers amongst the Fatui. Even so, I'm still unclear as to how he has been able to wield such a profound influence over Irminsul.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I can confirm that Fatui forces have arrived in Sumeru City.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Furthermore, Irminsul seems to be undergoing some kind of mutation. Evil branches are beginning to grow... Things that do not belong to this world are slowly but surely... materializing.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Sorry — I couldn't think of any other word to describe it. They don't seem to be fully formed physical entities yet, after all, but they are gradually becoming real.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: A baleful tree, climbing up into the heavens...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Speaking of Dottore, I have some information on that front as well.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Wanderer recounts how he and Paimon went to the meeting spot, only to find no one waiting for them.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I didn't think it was wise to state this out in the open. But my theory is, the mole wasn't cut off after he was caught. They wrote him off from the beginning.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: You mean, the Fatui never intended to follow through with him? Then why plant a mole at all?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: It's hardly a conventional strategy, and the rationale behind it is pretty twisted.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: But as it happens, I know someone who works exactly this way. And when it comes down to it, his goals are very simple... He just wants to confuse people, so they can't figure out what he's up to.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: He's been a collaborator of Dottore's from the outset. That fact alone confirms that Dottore is involved with this somehow.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Some people gasp upon hearing this name, while others fall silent. Clearly, there is more going on here than anyone realized.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Nahida proceeds to summon all relevant parties for a lengthy and in-depth meeting.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Nahida gives a detailed explanation of the enemy and the potential scale of the crisis.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After further intel provided by Nicole and Nefer, a plan is formulated and everyone prepares to get to work.

dialogues.speaker: Aradashan
dialogues.text: Wah! The Nara are looking this way!

dialogues.speaker: Arayuta
dialogues.text: Uh-oh, uh-oh...

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: It's okay. It's okay.

dialogues.speaker: Arabalika
dialogues.text: Arabalika will protect you all.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Do you hear that? Sounds like your teacher is scolding mine.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Heh, classic.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Did you see her? She's a former Vahumana student who dropped out of the Akademiya and went to Nod-Krai to work as an intel broker. There's more to her than meets the eye.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: How can you tell? Do the matra have information on her?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Some, but nothing telling. I'm basing it on the fact that she seems to be an expert liar. She can fool many with her words.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: A sixth sense for liars after investigating so many of them, I take it?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Yup. What about you? What do you make of her?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: A little earlier, in the corner, I noticed she gave some supplies to Jeht and had her deliver them to the main group.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: She's meticulous, and highly observant.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Besides, what was it you said? Making it to the top is no easy feat in any profession. Anyone who's at the top of their game has to have some sort of edge over others.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: It's true. But she's not the only one at the top of her game. I also am, and so are you.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Sure, but what's to guarantee she won't overhear us talking about her?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I have my methods. Sethos is distracting her.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Ah, I see.
